Given these points, the move bishop from d5 to a2 (UCI "d5a2") is both legal and forces the White king into check.

make_move d5a2

For example, moving our knight from d5 to e3 (written in UCI as “d5e3”) gives check. Notice that a knight on e3 would attack squares including g2—which is where White’s king sits—and forces White to make an immediate decision.

One tactical possibility after 1...d5e3+ is that if White decides to capture the knight with the queen (2.Qxe3), we can then have our knight on g4 jump into action by capturing that queen with 2...gxNe3 (i.e. “g4xe3”) since the knight from g4 can also reach e3. This sequence wins significant material in exchange—a knight (value ~3) for a queen (value ~9). (Of course, White may try alternative king moves to avoid the trade. However, in many lines, we end up with a beneficial imbalance.)
